transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Gritty bits on dishes usually mean water isn't reaching everything properly or debris is circulating back onto your plates. The most common cause is a dirty filter at the bottom of the tub, which traps food but can get clogged and restrict flow. 1. Take out the bottom rack and twist/lift out the filter at the base of the tub. Is it clogged with food or grit? (Rinse it under a tap if so.
2. Turn each spray arm by hand—does it spin freely, and are the little jet holes clear?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did the filter, its full of food n grease. spray arms: lower one spins fine but the upper 1 is stiff

That stiff upper arm is very likely why your glasses aren't getting clean; if it can't spin freely or its jets are blocked, that part of the tub won't get washed. Please unplug the machine again and try to remove the upper spray arm (usually by twisting it counter-clockwise) so you can rinse out any grit from inside it. To find the exact part for your Beko, could you read me the model number from the sticker on the side edge of the door?
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
dont know the model no, cant be bothered looking tbh, why do u need it? ill try take the arm off n rinse it tho

[Heading: Likely cause: spray arm]
I don't actually need the model number to help you fix this right now; I only asked because it helps me find the exact replacement part if the spray arm is broken. Since your upper arm is stiff, that's probably why your dishes aren't getting clean—water isn't reaching them properly. Please try removing the upper arm (usually by twisting it) and rinsing out any grit from the jets. If it's cracked or still won't spin after cleaning, we'll know it needs replacing.
ok took the arm off n rinsed it, a few holes were blocked with seeds n limescale so i poked them clear w a cocktail stick. its spinning better now

[Heading: Likely cause: spray arm]
That sounds like a great fix. The gritty bits and poor cleaning were almost probably caused by that stiff upper arm not spinning properly because of the seeds and limescale blocking the jets. Now that it's clear and moving freely again, your dishes should come out much cleaner. To help stop this happening too soon, try scraping off large food scraps before loading and give those spray arms a quick spin check every few months. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
